parts:

I hope I am not missing something obvious here, but this is perplexing to me.
Essentially, I constructed a boxplot with many outliers, such that the features
of the boxplots are difficult to see. Before thinking about transformations, I
simply wanted to "zoom in" on the boxplot portions, so I tried adjusting the y
axis limits using scale_y_continuous. However, the new labels on the y-axis do
not appear to agree with what they should be given the data. Am I
misunderstanding something about how scale_y_continuous works, or could this be
a bug?

I give a (long) reproducible data.frame with dput, because I know it displays
the behavior I discuss above. Sorry I don't have a more compact example!

Hi:

Compare the number of missing values in the two graphs:
> (p1 <- ggplot(data = testDF, aes(x = visit, y = value, colour = trt)) +

+  geom_boxplot())
Warning message:
Removed 166 rows containing missing values (stat_boxplot).

> p1 + scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0,250))
Warning message:
Removed 289 rows containing missing values (stat_boxplot).

# Now look at the subset of values <= 250:
> testDF2 <- subset(testDF, value <= 250)
> with(testDF2, tapply(value, list(trt, visit), median, na.rm = TRUE))
            Baseline Month 4 Month 12
Treatment A      128     105      112
Treatment B      130     146      133

They look compatible with the second graph to me...

HTH,

The answer to your question is coord_cartesian(), but I played around with the y-axis breaks so that the zoomed figure would have some semblance of a y-scale.

# First try:
p1 <- ggplot(data = testDF, aes(x = visit, y = value, colour = trt)) +

geom_boxplot()

# a little better.

p2 <- ggplot(data = testDF, aes(x = visit, y = value, colour = trt)) +
     geom_boxplot() + scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 3800, by = 100))
p2 + coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 250))

parts:
Hi,

coord_cartesian also has a "wise" parameter. When you set it to TRUE,
it should adjust the axis on its own (if I recall correctly)

p1 <- ggplot(data = testDF, aes(x = visit, y = value, colour = trt)) +
geom_boxplot()

p1 + coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 250), wise = TRUE)

Randolf
